entries.label: Real cost of capital tied up during a delay (also the required return in the user cost of capital)

citation.title: Cost Benefit Analysis (guidance note)
citation.publisher: Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, July 2023 (marked as under review)

entries.quote: OIA requires the calculation of net present values at an annual real discount rate of 7 per cent. … in addition to the 7 per cent ‘central’ discount rate, the net present values should also be calculated with real discount rates of 3 per cent and 10 per cent.
entries.derivation: Value = the OIA's central real discount rate (7%); low and high = its two sensitivity rates (3% and 10%).
entries.notes: The OIA rate is a social discount rate for net present values, not a measured cost of capital. Using it as the cost of capital tied up during a delay (F-C2-01) and as the required return r in the user cost (F-C3-01) is the tool's assumption, so the entry is graded D (traceability F-C2-01; interpretation A-P13). No Australian estimate of firms' real required return was verified for the library. The OIA note also accepts a central rate of 8% (p. 10, footnote 5).

entries.label: Holding cost of capital raised for a delayed clean-energy project (sensitivity)
entries.units: share of capital raised, a year (0.05 = 5%)

citation.title: Investing in cheaper, cleaner energy and the net zero transformation
citation.publisher: Productivity Commission, Inquiry report No. 113, 10 December 2025
citation.locator: p. 40 (PDF p. 48), 'The economic benefits of faster approvals'

entries.quote: We also heard that if a developer has raised $400 million, a one-year delay can cost upwards of $20 million in holding and opportunity costs (QREC, qr. 40, p. 4).
entries.derivation: Value = $20 million ÷ $400 million = 5% a year (derived). The source gives one figure ("upwards of"), so the range is the tool's ±50% rule (F-U-02).
entries.notes: A single stakeholder report (QREC) quoted by the PC, so an anecdote for one project type rather than an estimate; graded C. "Upwards of" means 5% is a floor for that project. Kept as a sensitivity on the OIA rate, as in the plan (§6.2 C2).
